review_note: Preserves locality of Cohen–Macaulay property (locally Noetherian with depth equal to local dimension) for syntomic coverings, in both directions of descent/ascent.
statement: Fix a nonnegative integer $k$ when the named property involves $(S_k)$ or $(R_k)$. Let $S$ be a scheme. The property "Cohen–Macaulay" (meaning the scheme is locally Noetherian and every local ring has depth equal to its Krull dimension) is local for the syntomic topology: for every syntomic covering $\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$, the scheme $S$ has this property if and only if every member $S_i$ has it.
hypotheses: S is a scheme; k is fixed when relevant; {S_i→S} is a syntomic covering.
conclusions: The property "Cohen–Macaulay" holds on S exactly when it holds on all covering schemes S_i.
